_comment: THE cross-language color contract. Go, TypeScript and elisp each assert
their own table against this file, row for row, which is the only
mechanism that makes a divergence between the three fail loudly instead
of quietly.
It pins WHICH of the five colors a state takes, not what that color's
value is: each renderer keeps its own hex, because a tab-bar background
and a CSS dot legitimately want different shades of the same idea. What
may never differ is the ASSIGNMENT — a workspace that reads green in one
surface and red in another is the failure this file exists to prevent.
'none' is a real answer, not a gap. The merge states deliberately carry
glyphs instead of colors so they never spend one of the five, and a
workspace with no session has no lifecycle verdict to paint. A surface
may override 'none' per state — see 'surface_overrides' — but only by
DECLARING the override here.
THERE IS NO TEAL. Teal existed solely to hold hibernation apart from a
broken substrate; hibernation left the contract, and with it the sixth
color. Blue means something about the route to a working session is
actually wrong, and it no longer carries a benign second job.
STATES ARE NAMED BY THEIR frontend.v1 ONEOF ARMS, not by a RENDER_STATE
enum. The daemon resolves every view, so the arm the daemon sets IS the
state a renderer paints, and there is no second spelling to keep aligned
by hand.
_precedence_comment: The five-color precedence, strongest claim first. Each color is a
strictly stronger claim about what the user CANNOT do than the one
beneath it, so the strongest true claim wins.
Blue leads because a compromised route to a session denies everything
else; purple is the vendor or the account refusing; red is the agent
holding the turn; yellow is detached work the user can talk over; green
is the session yours to use.
_roster_status_comment: Keyed by the RosterRow.status oneof arm names in
frontend/v1/sidebar.proto, spelled EXACTLY as the proto spells them.
A consumer asserts this map row for row against the proto's arm set:
every arm must appear here and every key here must be an arm, so a new
arm landing without a color fails the assertion instead of drawing an
The merge arms take 'none' — the roster draws them with the glyphs in
'merge_glyphs' rather than spending a lifecycle color on the merge
pipeline. 'none' and 'inactive' take 'none' because a workspace with no
session has no lifecycle to report at all.
'turn_failed' is BLUE (owner ruling, 2026-09-28). It is a turn end like
'done' and 'interrupted', and it holds the row as an unread result the
same way, but the turn did not produce what it was asked for, so it is
drawn in the color that says something is wrong rather than green.
_merge_glyphs_comment: GLYPH NAMES, not characters. The merge arms take no color, so the glyph
is the whole report, and each renderer maps these names to whatever its
surface can actually draw — a webapp icon, an Emacs character. What is
shared is WHICH glyph a merge state gets, never the character.
Keyed by the merge arms of RosterRow.status. 'feed_merge_head_glyph' is
separate because it names FeedMergeGlyph.icon on the feed's merge
bubble head, which reports the merge as a whole rather than one of its
_footer_status_comment: Keyed by the FooterStatus.status oneof arm names in
frontend/v1/footer.proto. The footer speaks about ONE session, so its
assignments answer a narrower question than the roster's, and the two
tables differ where the questions differ: footer 'merging' is purple
(the system holds this session, and the footer has no glyph to say so),
where a merging ROSTER row is 'none' and reports itself with a glyph.
'blocked' IS BLUE, like 'disconnected' and 'closing': a blocked session
cannot proceed until something outside it changes — a logged-out
account, a usage limit, a persistent vendor failure, a daemon that
cannot serve it — and every such state renders the agent unusable,
which is exactly what blue means. It reads the same as the roster's
'vendor_blocked', and the two are held together by ONE classifier so
the strip and the dot can never disagree about the same failure.
_footer_allowance_comment: The rate-limit allowance rung's status arms (frontend.v1 FooterAllowance.status,
sourced from SessionUpdate.rate_limit_status): allowed is quiet, allowed_warning
is the newsworthy rung, rejected means the vendor refused. Consumers assert row
for row against the three arm names; no private fallback table exists anywhere.
_topbar_connectivity_comment: TopbarConnectivity.tone, keyed by the daemon's link states. The topbar
reports the route to the session's shim, so its whole range is green
(serving), blue (the route is compromised) and 'none' (there is no
session to have a route to).
topbar.proto's comment on the `tone` field still lists teal. THE
COMMENT IS STALE and this file is authoritative: teal is not a value
any producer may emit, and 'topbar_tones' is the closed set a consumer
_surface_overrides_comment: A surface may paint a state differently from the shared assignment
above, but ONLY by naming the divergence here. Undeclared drift is
exactly what this file exists to prevent, so the escape hatch is a
declaration rather than a silent local table: a reader of any one
renderer still learns from this file that the surfaces disagree, and
each renderer asserts its own overrides against this section row for
row. A surface absent from this map takes 'roster_status' verbatim.
EMACS_TAB_BAR OVERRIDES THE THREE IN-FLIGHT MERGE ARMS TO PURPLE. The
tab bar has no glyphs — state reaches it only as the [N] bracket's
COLOR — so 'none' there means a workspace whose merge is running
renders exactly like one nobody has touched. Purple says what is true
of it: work is in flight, it is the SYSTEM's rather than the agent's,
and the user cannot act on the workspace until it resolves. Red would
have claimed a TURN was running, and a merging workspace's turn ended
before its merge began.
The three are the merge arms with no verdict yet: merge_enqueuing,
merge_queued and merging. merge_conflict, merge_failed and merged are
deliberately NOT overridden — a conflict wants the user, and the other
two are terminal, so none of them is 'in flight'.
vendor_blocked TAKES NO OVERRIDE ANY MORE. It once needed one because it
was purple in the shared table and the glyph-less tab bar could not tell
two purples apart, so it borrowed blue here. It is now blue in the
shared assignment itself — every way the route to a working session is
compromised is blue, and an auth wall, a usage limit or a persistent
vendor failure is precisely that — so the tab bar inherits blue with
nothing to declare. An override that paints an arm the color it already
has is not a divergence, and this file admits only real divergences.
The webapp takes NO overrides. Its rail carries a glyph and a status
word beside every dot, so 'none' already reads as the merge pipeline
reporting itself.
_failure_sides_comment: The SIDES of a failure — failure.proto's own vocabulary, which replaced
the old error classes. A failure card takes the color of the side it
lands on: card color IS state color, from this one table, so a user
cannot see a purple workspace explained by a blue card.
machinery is agent-repl's own machinery being compromised and
client_local is the client's end of the same route; both are blue,
because both mean the route to a working session is broken and neither
is the vendor's doing. vendor is purple: the vendor or the account has
stopped the work, and nothing in agent-repl is wrong.
